feasibility_reasoning:
The contract points the right way, and the hero keeps a stable DOM node: key={i} at sliderVariants.tsx:1198, and OptimizedImage.tsx:63,78,121 has no load-opacity state and computes sizes deterministically. But the mechanism as written has five holes.
(1) The primary signal "load, then decode(), then one rAF" runs inside the rAF callback, which comes before that frame's paint and presentation. decode() of the ~38 KB hero usually resolves before the first frame that paints it. So the burst starts a few ms before the LCP presentation timestamp, which contradicts the change's own verification ("every Script request starts after the observed LCP"). Lantern keeps any network node that ended before the cutoff (trace_engine lantern FirstContentfulPaint.js:104). Scripts with no EvaluateScript before the cutoff, or none at all, stay billed (:46-65). That covers modulepreloaded chunks.
(2) "LCP observer, first entry" as a racing fallback fires on the text candidate. With font-display: swap (styles.css:41,52), text paints at FCP before the hero; prod obs FCP is 3252 ms and obs LCP 3303 ms. At about 1.7 KB/ms observed, that window can bill up to about 85 KB of JS. The fixture cannot detect this, because there FCP = LCP. The observer must match entry.element[data-lcp-candidate] or entry.url === candidate.currentSrc, and decode() rejection needs a catch.
(3) The listed files cannot carry it. BOOT_PROBE_SCRIPT is a static, allowlisted literal (bootProbeScript.ts:79, dangerousHtmlAllowlist.ts:28-30) rendered in the React tree inside the entry chunk (__root.tsx:931). Embedding the hashed entry URL in it would create a content-hash cycle. The dictionary and widget URLs are per request (__root.tsx:531-532,743). The entry script comes from the TanStack manifest and <Scripts>. The change therefore also needs a manifest rewrite, injection outside the React tree, and removal of JS from Link in __root.tsx, rootHead.ts:94 and widgetPreloads.ts:25, not only frameworkPreloads.server.ts:14-17. router.tsx:210 is only kept. Effort is M to L, not S.
(4) The named gates (entry-purity, chunks, chunk-parity) are unaffected. What actually breaks is e2e/boot-home.spec.ts:26-29, e2e/boot-timing.spec.ts:961-975 and bootProbeScript.test.ts.
(5) The host injects /~flock.js (8.4 KB, defer, not in src), so "nothing before LCP except CSS, font, hero" cannot hold on prod.
There is also a hard dependency on LP-1's marker: without it the trigger degrades to DCL+rAF, which leaks JS before LCP.
